a novel pathogenic mutation in the SMC1A gene, c.298+2T>C, was detected. She was diagnosed with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.

This patient did not exhibit bathing seizures after stopping her bathing but later experienced frequent spontaneous and drug-resistant seizures. The interictal EEG background slowed down, while focal epileptic discharge increased. Her intellectual development was significantly delayed, and a novel pathogenic mutation in the SMC1A gene, c.298+2T>C, was detected.
